questions.q: Why did Kendall's grandmother not consider herself a feminist?
a: She felt feminism mainly looked out for white women
She believed women should not work outside the home
She thought feminism ignored the needs of men
She had never heard of the women's movement
questions.why: Lesson 1 says her grandmother, a woman of color, saw feminism as a movement that served white women.

questions.q: Which needs does Kendall say mainstream feminism tends to overlook?
a: Poverty, hunger and secure housing
Access to birth control and reproductive care
Equal pay and workplace advancement
Representation in film and advertising
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues feminists focus on issues like birth control while many women struggle for food, housing and health care.

Arguing that prisons should be abolished entirely
Focusing feminism only on economic inequality
Treating feminism as a matter of personal choice
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines carceral feminism as the assumption that police and punishment will deliver justice for victims.

questions.q: Why can involving the police make things worse for some minority women?
a: They may lose income or even face charges themselves
Police usually refuse to investigate their cases at all
Courts rarely allow them to testify in trials
Their communities punish them for reporting violence
questions.why: Lesson 2 says survivors may be left without income, and women who defend themselves can end up prosecuted.

questions.q: What separates an accomplice from an ally, according to Kendall?
a: An accomplice takes action even when it brings no personal benefit
An ally speaks publicly while an accomplice works privately
An accomplice focuses on charity rather than politics
An ally challenges bias while an accomplice avoids conflict
questions.why: Lesson 3 says accomplices act against white supremacy and defend marginalized communities regardless of personal gain.
